# Check of M0-a-07 — the face partitioners (lane `check/M0-a-07`, flow flow-7, stage group 8, 2026-10-05)

Lane `check/M0-a-07` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on the owner's Windows 11 PC (WSL2 Ubuntu, Linux x64,
Node 24.12.0) on 2026-10-05, from about 00:55 to 02:10. This seat is an implementer-side independent checker of item
M0-a-07. It is not the item's author (`build/M0-a-07`, ledger rows L-0144 and L-0152). The seat changed no file of the
item and ran no git command. It ran one vitest process at a time: `--maxWorkers=2` for the gates, and `--maxWorkers=1`
for the mutants and probes. `free -m` showed about 10 – 12 GB available before each run. The mutants and probes ran in
a scratch mirror of `plat/`, which was deleted afterwards along with its node_modules. Logs are in the session
scratchpad's `build/a07-*.log`. Every receipt this verdict rests on is quoted here. Timings are CONTENDED and are not
a result. The checker's ledger row is **L-0158**, and the minor notes are in `checks/M0-a-07-notes.md` (N-1 – N-6).

## Verdict: FAIL — one blocker (B-1); every gate is green

| line | finding | label |
|---|---|---|
| **B-1** | A targeted mutant on §3.6's sliver rule survives the item's whole test set, B-FUZZ included. The rule says "the sliver stays as a face of kind `residue` owned by the neighbour across its longest boundary". M15 (`merge.ts` line 169: `near[0].face` → `near[near.length - 1].face`, so the owner comes from the shortest boundary) survived the deterministic files and also survived with `bfuzz.test.ts` at 2000 runs. The only residue test (`merge.test.ts`, "a sliver between a spine and a shore keeps both") has one owned neighbour, so it cannot tell the longest boundary from any other. On the real code the owner is right: probe P12 passes, and P12 kills M15 (`AssertionError: expected 4 to be 3`). So the item's behaviour is correct, but the test for this design clause cannot fail. | CONFIRMED |

**Required change (fix round `build/M0-a-07-fix1`):** add a test to `packages/kernel/test/faces/merge.test.ts` in which
the sliver below its floor has two owned neighbours across structural boundaries of different lengths, and which
asserts that the residue takes the owner across the longer one. Probe P12 is such a fixture and can be copied as it
stands:

```ts
const p = halves();
commit(p, 1, (o) => insertChain(o, pts([[0, 1900], [3000, 1900], [3000, 2000]]), [{ role: 'way', entity: 'way:7' }], 'mandatory'));
const s = faceAt(p, 1, 1500, 1950); const lower = faceAt(p, 1, 1500, 500); const upper = faceAt(p, 1, 1500, 3000);
commit(p, 1, (o) => { const a = setOwner(o, [lower], 'block:low'); if (!a.ok) return a; return setOwner(o, [upper], 'block:up'); });
const c = commit(p, 1, (o) => absorbSliver(o, s, { minWidthCm: 200, minAreaCm2: 0 }));
expect(c.value).toBe(s);
expect(p.faces[1].owner[s]).toBe(p.faces[1].owner[lower]);   // 3 100 cm shared with `lower`, 3 000 cm with `upper`
```

Then re-run M15 and confirm the new test kills it. No source change is needed.

### Targeted mutants (32, run one at a time in the mirror, `--maxWorkers=1`)

Each mutant was aimed at a promise the item states: a §3.6 contact rule, the children's order, the record keeper,
E_HOLE_CONTACT, the sliver rule, E_STRUCTURAL and E_LEVEL, the pin's level and count, the work charge, the claim's
spanning and its `collapsed` refusal, the fan's order, its single-ray refusal and its atomicity, and the band's
refusals. Each pattern matched exactly once, and the file was restored after each run. Against the item's
deterministic files (split, hole, merge, fan, claim, limits, source):

* **25 KILLED:** M04 – M14, M16 – M25, M27, M28, M30, M31.
* **7 SURVIVED:** M01, M02, M03, M15, M26, M29, M32.

The survivors M01, M02, M15, M29 and M32 were then re-run with `bfuzz.test.ts` at `PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS=2000`.
`M01 vertex rule radius: KILLED`, `M02 interior pt near edge radius: KILLED` (N-2: held by the fuzz only);
`M15 residue owner longest: SURVIVED` (**B-1**); M29 and M32 SURVIVED (equivalent, N-5). M03 is equivalent, because
the minEdge check refuses the same cut with the same code (N-5). M26 is a boundary-only survivor (N-4).

### Probes (12, scratch vitest file in the mirror; all green on the item's code)

* P1: a graze 28.3 cm from the reflex vertex splits, and one 14.1 cm from it is refused.
* P6: splitFace on an own-child region (an L2 batch, `faceLevel: 1`), then the merge returns −1 and the arena is valid.
* P7: an end whose foot lies within `attractCm` of a corner lands on the corner.
* P8: an end 10 cm off an edge lands at its foot, and the children tile the parent exactly.
* P9: split ∘ merge on a holed face restores the ring and the id.
* P10: after connectHole, `mergeFaces(g, g)` is E_DEGENERATE.
* P11: a sliver between two ways is retyped residue.
* P12: the residue owner comes from the longest boundary, and P12 kills M15.

These are attempts to refute the item on honest inputs, and none found a wrong result.
